text: dysenteriae has been reported.2 Fluoroquinolones are generally not used in children, although a study9 in Bangladesh has used ciprofloxacin in children with shigellosis and found it to be of similar efficacy to pivmecillinam. In studies from Israel, the third-generation cephalosporins ceftriaxone10 or cefixime11 were more effective than ampicillin or co-tri- moxazole, respectively, in children with shigellosis. Other studies in adults in Bangladesh found cefixime to be inef- fective compared with pivmecillinam12 and azithromycin to be effective, although slightly less so, than cipro- floxacin.13 Rifaximin has also been investigated.2 Vitamin A may be a useful adjunct to treatment, especially in children in developing countries (see Diarrhoea, under Vitamin A, p.1973).
